scene: Inferno XXXII — frozen Cocytus, Caina, Antenora, constrained bodies and contested identities
story: Dante and Virgil walk upon the frozen lake of Cocytus at the bottom of the ninth circle, where the souls of traitors are fixed in the ice.

In Caina, betrayers of family protrude from the lake; the brothers Alessandro and Napoleone degli Alberti are trapped close together. Their tears freeze and their heads strike one another. Camicione de' Pazzi identifies them.
In Antenora, traitors of homeland or party are frozen further in, with only parts of their faces exposed. Dante strikes a trapped soul with his foot and demands his name.
Bocca degli Abati refuses to identify himself. Dante pulls his hair, and another soul names Bocca; the identity is revealed through another speaker, not initially confirmed by Bocca's own testimony.
Bocca in turn names other traitors. His accusations and the other soul's disclosure must remain attributed to their speakers.
At the close Dante observes two souls together in one hollow, one gnawing the head of the other. Their story and identities as Ugolino and Ruggieri are developed in Canto XXXIII.
No trapped figure is released; physical immobilization and identity attribution remain separate issues.

cipher.operator: FREEZE -> CONTAIN -> OBSERVE -> QUESTION -> RESIST -> ATTRIBUTE
invariants: Physical immobility does not erase a person's distinct narrative identity
Partial visibility does not establish a person's identity without additional attribution
Refusing to self-identify is distinct from being unnamed by another speaker
An observer's coercive action is not independent proof of the claim it tries to obtain
Two figures sharing one hollow need not share identity, intent or testimony
The end-of-canto pair is observed but not yet explained; do not import their full account early
